Shorten the segment about going to Audrey's dressing room as it's not crucial to the main point.

text_to_speech: we did this all in a day and a half Mr Gleason said comedy is not funny if it's over rehearsed and boy we weren't over reversed we wouldn't get the scripts delivered to our apartments on Thursday and on Friday we can go into the office and get the changes that Jackie had made overnight and then we'd show up 11 o'clock Saturday morning at CBS Studio 50 which they now call The Ed Sullivan Theater we really just did one dress rehearsal on Saturday afternoon and went on live that night which is utterly unbelievable but that's the way Jackie wanted it and it worked but after the dress rehearsal we'd all run up to Audrey's dressing room except Jackie he ran off into his own dressing room perhaps he was studying we don't know and we would run over the script many times with Audrey's manager Val Reading in Jackie's lines and that helped us get through that night at eight o'clock when that red light went on it you knew Millions were watching and then you were so under rehearsed but it worked how scary was that it was very scary I mean I was really almost glad that I didn't have very much to do

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: We did this all in a day and a half.
Mr. Lee said comedy is not funny if it's overrehearsed.
And while we weren't overrehearsed,
we wouldn't get the script delivered to our apartments on Thursday.
And on Friday, we'd go into the office
and get the changes that Jackie had made overnight.
And then we'd show up 11 o'clock Saturday morning
at just CBS Studio 50, which they now call the Ed Sullivan Theater.
We really just did one dress rehearsal on Saturday afternoon.
And when I live that night, which is utterly unbelievable,
but that's the way Jackie wanted it.
And it worked.
But after the dress rehearsal,
we'd all run up to Audrey's dressing room.
Except Jackie, he ran off into his own dressing room.
Perhaps he was studying.
We don't know.
And we would run over the script many times
with Audrey's manager, Val, reading in Jackie's lines.
And that helped us get through that night at 8 o'clock.
When that red light went on,
it, you knew millions were watching and end.
And you were so underrehearsed, but it worked.
How scared was that?
It was very scary.
I mean, I was really almost glad
that I didn't have very much to do.
